A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoRA research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, tables and figures can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original MoRA results for CLIP continual learning, T5 task sequences and Llama3.1-8B fine-tuning, together with ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds LLaMA2-7B experiments, another X-TAIL task order, additional comparisons and measured GPU memory use.

M1.justification: Rank-one experts, incremental addition and freezing, activation-derived routing, top-k selection, temperature scaling and inference thresholding are retained. V2 explains these operations more explicitly; v1 Section 4.5 already specifies test-time pruning, so this is not a newly introduced procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MTIL/X-TAIL image datasets, standard and 15-task language streams, CodeAlpaca, HumanEval and MMLU coverage. LLaMA2-7B changes the evaluated model, and X-TAIL Order 2 rearranges retained tasks; neither introduces new represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 adds InfLoRA to the T5 and X-TAIL comparisons, LoRI-D and LoRI-S to HumanEval, and a Fine-tune reference row to Table 1. These extend the existing comparisons. Router@LoRA and Router@rank are renamed MoE-LoRA and Non-self-activation, with their scores retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds a LLaMA2-7B configuration, another X-TAIL task order, HumanEval Pass@5/Pass@10 evaluation and measured resource comparisons within retained coverage. Section 4 also revises Average from the mean of Transfer and Last to mean accuracy across datasets and learning stages. This reported metric revision does not establish that the unchanged earlier results were recomputed.

E4.justification: V1 Table 5 combines temperature scaling and the activation budget in one Sparse activation row. V2 Table 4 replaces it with separate top-k, sharpness-control and test-time-thresholding variants. Together with new task-order robustness tests and measured parameter/memory analyses in Tables 14–15, this substantially expands the diagnostic evidence. Existing sensitivity plots and activation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 states that results average three independent runs but supplies no standard deviations. V2 Table 13 adds mean and standard deviation reporting for InfLoRA, CoDyRA and MoRA over three runs. This adds uncertainty information for a subset of comparisons without establishing additional runs or formal significance tests; v1's blanket run-count disclosure is no longer present.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include LLaMA2-7B average accuracy of 78.4 versus O-LoRA's 76.1, MoRA HumanEval Pass@5/Pass@10 of 60.9/70.1, and X-TAIL Order 2 Transfer/Average/Last scores of 59.5/69.3/80.7. V2 also adds comparator, ablation and GPU-memory results. Existing X-TAIL, MTIL, code/MMLU and long-sequence T5 scores are retained; standard T5 score edits are equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The associative-memory derivations move from v1 Appendix A into v2 Sections 3.2–3.3 with equivalent mathematics. A limited formula revision occurs in Table 10: CoDyRA's parameter count changes from r(d_in+d_out) to r(d_in+d_out)+r, although v2's computation-cost prose retains the old expression. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The main claims about rank-level adaptation, forgetting mitigation, generalization and parameter efficiency remain. V2 drops the introduction's categorical assertion that the design introduces no additional computation and instead emphasizes avoiding extra router parameters, modestly narrowing the computational claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of how selection and temperature affect learning signals and why thresholding is restricted to inference. It also interprets the new robustness and memory results. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit warning that thresholds above 0.2 degrade performance and its discussion of sparse-update misuse and persistent biases; the underlying sensitivity figure remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds the MTIL class count, the rationale for excluding CIFAR100 from X-TAIL, and details of adapter configurations used in resource comparisons. It removes v1's RTX 3090 and four-H100 hardware disclosure. Existing training hyperparameters and the promise to release code upon acceptance remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references covering LoRI, Mixture of LoRA Experts, MoE theory for continual learning, S2FT and Llama 2, while removing Wang et al.'s comprehensive continual-learning survey. Its introduction more carefully distinguishes fixed-expert, expanding-expert and task-specific-router designs. The central positioning against coarse adapter-level routing remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, method exposition and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting and restructuring. V1's method appendix is integrated into the main text, gating operations receive separate explanations, MTIL discussion moves to the appendix, and the experimental appendix is reorganized. V2 also introduces an LLM-use statement and switches to author-date citations.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 9 and 12–15, expands existing comparison tables, redesigns the ablation table and relocates MTIL results from Table 2 to appendix Table 11. Figure 4 is reduced and placed beside the ablation table, with broader template and layout changes. All nine figure graphics are retained. New Table 13 has dataset headers inconsistent with the MoRA/CoDyRA means repeated from Table 1.

improvement.justification: The separated component ablations, additional model and task-order tests, relevant comparators, and measured memory and uncertainty reporting provide useful additional support for the retained method. Integrating the method explanation also improves accessibility. The gain is limited by Table 13's mismatched dataset headers, removal of explicit hardware information and the inconsistent CoDyRA parameter count between Table 10 and its prose. Overall, the added validation and clarity support a modest net improvement.
